subject_line: Miracle Whip and the gods of To the Refrigerator Gods
email_body:
Dear Terry,

I came across To the Refrigerator Gods, your Seven Kitchens Press chapbook, and was struck by how seriously and playfully your poems take food, from "O Miracle Whip" to the "Macaroni & Cheese Survey" that appeared in Gastronomica. I would love to ask how the kitchen became such a steady source of poems for you, and how teaching creative writing in Indianapolis feeds that work.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Food-centered poems (To the Refrigerator Gods, Seven Kitchens Press 2010; poems in Gastronomica) per IU Indianapolis directory; email seen in search result from university directory.

subject_line: Choreography and the poems of Sylph
email_body:
Dear Abigail,

I was reading about Sylph, your Lena-Miles Wever Todd Prize collection from Pleiades Press, and about your background in dance and your interest in bringing choreography and poetry together. I would love to ask how a dancer's sense of the body and of movement in space finds its way into a line or a stanza, and how editing Mid-American Review has changed the way you read your own drafts.

book_title: The Book of Fools: An Essay in Memoir and Verse
subject_line: Plastic, oceans and The Book of Fools
email_body:
Dear Sam,

I was reading about The Book of Fools: An Essay in Memoir and Verse, which the Ulrich Museum described at its release reading as a sweeping elegy for the Earth and its plastic-choked oceans. Raised in Miami and now directing the MFA program in Wichita, you write about the sea from far inland. I would love to ask why this book needed both memoir and verse, and how you found its form.
